records.text: An unnamed audiovisual professional wrote that a second microphone would only make sense for a broadcast, recording, or livestream, because routing both microphones to a public-address system on different channels would cause interference, overlap, and echo.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #6 (Ep G3zdOeHpvS0)

appearances.snippet: The only reason for trolley to be rigged with two mics would be because one was One was being sent to a broadcast recording or a live stream had both his handheld mic and the road mic been used to run audio to the PA system at the school using different channels, this would cause a myriad of issues that would present with interference, overlapping and echo between the two channels.

verification.notes: Shure guidance confirms two active microphones on one source can create comb filtering and increase feedback risk. The unnamed source overstates that broadcast or recording is the only valid reason for redundancy, and separate channels do not inherently guarantee interference or echo.

sources.title: Shure Audio Systems Guide for Meetings and Conferences
sources.relevance: Explains multiple-microphone pickup, comb filtering, feedback risk, and the recommendation to keep only one presenter microphone active.
